blocks.content: Mr. Alvarez has a way of asking questions that find the exact thing you weren't planning to talk about. Not aggressively. He just — lands on it. Like he already knew where it was and was waiting for the right moment.
He said it the way you repeat a word when you know it's not the whole story.
You know what I put in your coffee?
Two sugars. Because bitterness should only exist in art.
He says that every time. I've decided it keeps being true, which is why he keeps saying it.
When do you paint something because you want to, not because someone asked?
I looked at the table for a second.
He made a sound — not agreement, not disagreement. The kind of sound that means you're right about the surface of something but you've missed the thing underneath it.

I've thought about that a lot. The painting I actually want to make. Most artists I've read about talk about it like something you work toward — you get close enough and it finds you. I don't know if I believe that. But I haven't stopped waiting for it either.
